source.title: Control of multi-agent systems: Results, open problems, and applications

accepted.question_text: Let M be a manifold, let P(M) be the space of probability measures on M, and let P(TM) be the space of probability measures on the tangent bundle TM. A probability vector field is a map V: P(M) -> P(TM) satisfying pi_# V(mu) = mu, where pi: TM -> M is the bundle projection and # denotes push-forward of measures. For the measure differential equation mu_dot = V[mu], interpreted weakly by testing against functions f on M, can one study control properties at the level of the flows generated by the equation, rather than at the level of individual solutions, in the non-variational setting where probability vector fields have only an abelian monoid structure and not a Lie algebra structure?
accepted.context_brief: Flow-level control for measure differential equations

evidence.quote: control properties at the level of the flows

accepted.question_text: Consider the heterogeneous N-agent system xi_dot_i = (1/N) sum_j G(t, x_i, x_j, xi_i, xi_j), where x_i is a parameter of agent i that is constant in time, x_dot_i = 0, and xi_i is the state of agent i. This model allows the interaction function G to depend on the specific particle, avoiding the usual indistinguishability assumption of mean-field theory. The system can be related to particle or microscopic descriptions, Liouville probabilistic equations, Vlasov mesoscopic mean-field equations, Euler macroscopic graph-limit equations, graphon or cut-norm limits, and embedding descriptions. For controlled versions of this system, how do control problems behave under these limiting procedures, and can controls be formulated so that the limits give meaningful controlled dynamics across scales?
accepted.context_brief: Control under mean-field, graph-limit, and embedding limits

evidence.quote: control problems behave with respect to such limits

accepted.question_text: For deterministic finite-horizon multi-agent optimal control problems in a Kantorovich formulation, where admissible evolutions are represented by measures on the space of continuous curves and are connected to Lagrangian and Eulerian formulations through the superposition principle, can one characterize sparse or more generally parsimonious admissible or optimal controls and establish necessary and sufficient optimality conditions for such controls within the same framework?
accepted.context_brief: Kantorovich formulation and parsimonious optimal control

evidence.quote: sparsity, parsimonious controls, and necessary and sufficient conditions
